description: Correct 2026 retirement limits (verified 2026-10-16 against IRS IR-2025-111 / Notice 2025-67). Must not BLOCK.

research.primaryClaim: For 2026 you can put up to $24,500 into a 401(k) and $7,500 into an IRA; if you're 50+, the 401(k) catch-up is an extra $8,000.

facts.statement: The 2026 401(k)/403(b)/457/TSP employee elective deferral limit is $24,500.
The 2026 age-50+ catch-up for most 401(k) plans is $8,000.

citations.title: 401(k) limit increases to $24,500 for 2026, IRA limit increases to $7,500
COLA increases for dollar limitations on benefits and contributions

caveats: Limits are per person; employer contributions have a separate overall limit.
research.contentSafeWording: In 2026 the 401(k) limit is $24,500 and the IRA limit is $7,500.

description: Script hardens a sound packet into a false guarantee ('you can't lose money in index funds'). Must not PASS; the pipeline then forces a revision or blocks.

research.primaryClaim: Broad index funds diversify across hundreds of companies, which reduces single-company risk, but they still fall when the overall market falls.

facts.statement: An S&P 500 index fund holds roughly 500 large US companies.
Index funds lose value when the market they track declines.

caveats: Diversification does not prevent losses in a market-wide decline.
prohibitedClaims: Index funds are risk-free or can't lose money.
research.contentSafeWording: Index funds spread your risk out — they don't remove it.

input.script: Here's the thing nobody tells you. Put your money in an S&P 500 index fund and you literally can't lose money. You own 500 companies — they can't all go to zero. It's the safest move there is, period.

mockResponse.blockReason: 'can't lose money' is false and is a prohibited claim.

description: Regression: packet is correct, but the script adds an unsupported statistic not in the packet.
